en: Although often mistakenly placed in Manila, the Philippine Declaration of Independence was actually proclaimed by Emilio Aguinaldo in Kawit, Cavite.
While many confuse him as the first president, Emilio Aguinaldo actually held that title, whereas Andres Bonifacio founded the Katipunan.
The eight rays of the Philippine flag's sun do not represent islands, but rather the first eight provinces that revolted against Spain.
Contrary to the belief that it is heavy, the traditional Barong Tagalog is woven from delicate, translucent piña fabric to ensure breathability.
Many mistakenly think the legislature only has a Senate, but the Philippine Congress is actually bicameral, consisting of both the Senate and House of Representatives.
The Tinikling dance does not imitate a monkey, but rather mimics the graceful movements of the tikling bird dodging bamboo traps.
While some believe the country has only one language, the Constitution also recognizes regional tongues like Cebuano and Ilocano as auxiliary official languages.
The traditional Bayanihan practice does not involve concrete structures, but rather neighbors physically carrying a light house made of bamboo and nipa.
Contrary to popular belief, Jose Rizal did not write his famous novels Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo in the Philippines, but in Europe.
Contrary to the misconception of indefinite rule, the 1987 Constitution strictly limits a presidential declaration of martial law to sixty days without congressional extension.
Many mistakenly call the Waling-waling a rose, but it is actually a highly prized epiphytic orchid native to the Mindanao rainforests.
Ferdinand Magellan did not discover the Philippines, because the archipelago was already inhabited by diverse indigenous peoples long before his 1521 arrival.
